question: Which specific manufacturers are approved by the MUTCD to supply retroreflective sign sheeting?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The MUTCD does not approve, endorse, or name any specific manufacturers of retroreflective sign sheeting. None of the provided evidence — nor the MUTCD generally — lists approved suppliers; instead, the Manual sets performance-based requirements for when and how signs must be retroreflective (e.g., regulatory, warning, and guide signs must be retroreflective or illuminated). Because the evidence contains no manufacturer approvals, the question cannot be answered as asked. Standards (mandatory): - "Regulatory, warning, and guide signs (see Section 2A.03), and object markers, shall be retroreflective or illuminated to show the same shape and similar color by both day and night, unless otherwise provided in this Manual for a particular sign or group of signs." — This is a performance requirement; no manufacturer is specified. - "Letters, numerals, symbols, arrows, and borders of all guide signs shall be retroreflective. The background of all guide signs that are not independently illuminated shall be retroreflective." — Again, no supplier is named. Visual evidence: [Image 4] Table 2A-4 lists generic "Means of Retroreflection" (e.g., prismatic reflector "buttons," materials with a smooth sealed outer surface over a light-reflecting microstructure) by material type, not by manufacturer, confirming that the MUTCD addresses retroreflection functionally rather than by brand. Citations: - Section 2A.21 Standard §3 (p.62) - Section 2E.10 Standard §1 (p.293) - Table 2A-4 (p.62)
